To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in Syrian hamster, there are separate subpopulations of GnRH-ir neurons associated with pulsatility and surge secretion of LH and that the expression of FOS-ir in these subpopulations of neurons is affected by estrous cycle phase and metabolic fuel availability.

in Syrian hamster females, GnRH neurons in the rostral forebrain express Fos-IR during proestrus, when the GnRH pulse generator is activated, but GnRH neurons in more caudal regions express Fos- IR during the entire cycle, when the GnR H pulse generator is active.

food deprivation on day 1 and 4 of the estrous cycle, insulin, and 2-deoxy-d-glucose on day one of the cycle, all suppress the expression of FOS-like proteins in GnRH-immuno-reactive neurons of the Syrian hamster.

food deprivation reduces GnRH secretion by GnRH-IR cells in the caudoputamen, and this reduction in GnRH secretion may account for the nutritional infertility that is seen in female mammals.
